title: Non-blocking findings from PR #319's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings recorded by pr-reviewer's code-review/verify-elder-signal passes on PR #319, tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's same-calendar-day response cache (app.api.indicator_history_cache.IndicatorHistoryResponseCache) can serve a stale `trading_mode` field after the global trading mode changes between requests within the same calendar day: a cached IndicatorHistoryResponse's `trading_mode` is baked in at write time (app/api/routers/stocks.py's `cached_response = response_cache.get(ticker, range)` check returns the stored response as-is on a hit) and never refreshed to the freshly-resolved current setting. Narrow in practice -- only reachable while the swing branch is still being taken with a cache hit (e.g. day_trader mode configured with no triple yet, which is treated the same as swing), not once a fully-intraday triple is active (that always bypasses the cache entirely) -- but undocumented as an accepted tradeoff the way this same cache's OHLCV/signal staleness already is (see IndicatorHistoryResponse.points's own field description). Worth either invalidating/excluding this field from the cached payload and re-attaching the freshly-resolved trading_mode_setting_out on every cache hit, or explicitly documenting this as an accepted staleness case alongside the existing one.

GET /api/portfolio/risk's first-pass loop (app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_risk, the loop populating stops/weekly_by_id/daily_by_id) duplicates ~15 lines of near-identical logic (drop_malformed_daily_bars, the len<2 check, the protective_stop try/except ValueError) across the day_trader_active and swing branches, differing only in where daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv come from (day-trader legs already fetched concurrently up front vs. a per-position swing weekly fetch). A future fix to that shared sequence (a new guard, a different exception type) has to be applied in both places by hand -- worth factoring the shared drop_malformed_daily_bars/length-check/protective_stop steps into one helper taking (daily_ohlcv_raw, weekly_ohlcv) once each branch has resolved those two inputs its own way.

app.portfolio.risk.position_risk_pct's 'distance to stop' computation in day-trader mode mixes a swing-derived `current_price` (this ticker's ordinary EOD daily-chart close, per PortfolioResponse.trading_mode's own field description) with a day-trader-mode-derived `protective_stop` (computed from the active triple's IBKR-fetched intermediate leg) for the same position -- the resulting 2%-rule risk percentage spans two different data sources/timeframes for the same ticker rather than one live intraday price against a live intraday stop. This follows the already-reviewed backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk (PR #317) generalization precedent, not something introduced fresh by PR #319, but PR #319 is what makes it reachable end-to-end via the real GET /api/portfolio/risk endpoint with a real per-position IBKR fetch, and no `decisions` entry anywhere in this feature's chain addresses this specific current_price/stop timeframe mismatch. Worth deciding (and recording via `decisions`) whether this is an accepted tradeoff (matching current_price/equity's own already-documented 'always swing-derived regardless of mode' precedent) or worth a dedicated live-intraday-price fetch for this specific calculation in day-trader mode.

backend/tests/integration/test_portfolio_get.py's TestDayTraderMode class only exercises single-position scenarios (one PositionORM per test). The discriminating 'does the concurrent fan-out mix up which ticker gets which outcome' test exists at the unit level (tests/unit/api/test_day_trader_signal.py's test_maps_each_distinct_ticker_to_its_own_outcome_not_a_shared_or_swapped_one) but not as a GET /api/portfolio integration test with 2+ held positions of genuinely different tickers/outcomes -- worth adding one so a regression in how compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently's results get matched back to the right position in get_portfolio's own loop would be caught at the router-integration level too, not only at the day_trader_signal.py unit level.
